property_summary: After depositing an amount x for an account, the contract balance for that account is never less than x (i.e., deposit never causes the depositor's recorded balance to be smaller than the deposited value).
Calling deposit with any msg.value must never revert (i.e., deposit always succeeds) when msg.sender is any address.
If deposit is called with a positive Ether amount, the call must not revert when the caller has sufficient available Ether to send.

Depositing any positive amount from this test contract will never revert for a caller that has previously deposited enough to make balances[msg.sender]+value overflow in the mutant (i.e., deposit reverts iff msg.value is zero or caller lacks funds) — equivalently: for any value, if the test contract has enough balance to send it, deposit must not revert in the original but may revert in the mutant when wraparound would occur.

For any caller and deposit amount, if this contract can send that Ether then deposit does not revert when the caller's prior recorded balance is at least MAX_UINT256 - amount (i.e., deposit prevents wrapping on overflow).

For any depositor and any positive msg.value, calling deposit() always increases that depositor's recorded balance by exactly the deposited amount (i.e., balances[addr] after deposit >= balances[addr] before deposit and in absence of overflow balances_after == balances_before + amount); the mutant that removes the overflow check can wrap balances on large deposits and thus violates this for some inputs.

For any depositor and any deposit value, after calling deposit() the contract's recorded balance for that depositor is strictly less than 2**256 (i.e. no wraparound occurs) — the mutant that removes the overflow check allows wraparound so for some depositor and large msg.value the recorded balance becomes smaller than the deposited amount (wraps), violating the no-wrap property.

For any depositor and any two successive deposits by that same depositor, the second deposit never decreases the depositor's recorded balance compared to immediately after the first deposit; removing the overflow check allows the second deposit to cause wraparound and thus reduce the recorded balance for some inputs.

For any depositor and any deposit value where the depositor's prior recorded balance is zero, after a single deposit the recorded balance equals the sent msg.value (the mutant can wrap an extreme msg.value to zero when prior balance is zero, violating this).

For any depositor and any two deposit operations from two distinct senders that together overflow the depositor's balance when the second deposit is processed via a malicious intermediary that forwards funds, the reference ensures that a single depositor's balance never decreases across an intervening external call that could reenter/forward funds; the mutant (removing the assert) allows wraparound so there exist fuzzed inputs where after the sequence the depositor's recorded balance is smaller — the test constructs two senders and a forwarding helper to trigger a large combined addition and observes c.balances(depositor) decreased after the second deposit.
After depositing some positive ether from an address, that address's balance in the contract increases by at least the deposited amount.

property_summary: Calling deposit with a positive value should succeed (not revert) on the original contract but the mutant breaks the invariant that deposits with positive value always succeed.

For any caller and any positive msg.value, calling deposit() increases that caller's recorded balance by exactly the sent msg.value (so balances[msg.sender] after the call >= previous balance and increases by msg.value); the mutant that sets balances[msg.sender]=0 breaks this by making the balance not increase for many inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero deposit amount, after calling deposit() the contract's recorded balance for that caller increases (i.e., balances[caller] >= previous balance + msg.value); the mutant that assigns zero to balances breaks this by not increasing the recorded balance for some fuzzed amounts and callers.

For any caller and any nonzero ETH sent to deposit(), the caller's recorded balance (as read via the public balances getter) strictly increases compared to its previous value; the mutant that sets balances[msg.sender]=0 breaks this because some deposits leave the recorded balance unchanged or reset to zero.

For any caller and any nonzero sent ETH, after calling deposit() the contract's recorded balance for that caller is at least the amount sent (balances[caller] >= previous + msg.value); the mutant that assigns zero to balances breaks this because some deposits do not increase the stored balance.

For any caller and any nonnegative ETH amount, after calling deposit() the contract's recorded balance for that caller is not zero if a positive amount was sent—reference C always increases the caller's stored balance by adding msg.value (so it won't be zero when depositing >0), while the mutant that assigns zero breaks this by leaving the stored balance zero for some deposits.
After a deposit of v from this contract, the contract's recorded balance for the depositor increases by exactly v (i.e., balances[msg.sender] post - pre == v).
A deposit that sends value v from the caller never causes the contract to revert/assert (deposit always succeeds) for any prior balance and any v.
Calling deposit with any nonzero value never triggers an assertion failure (i.e., deposit does not assert) when the caller provides that value from this test contract.

For any caller and any prior balance, after calling deposit with value v the caller can always withdraw at least v (i.e., the contract's external balance for the caller increases by at least v and is withdrawable).

property_summary: Calling deposit with value v always increases the caller's withdrawable balance by exactly v (i.e., the contract's recorded balance for the caller after deposit is at least its prior value), so deposit never makes the stored balance decrease relative to its pre-call value.

For any caller and any nonzero deposit value that is sent successfully, after deposit() returns the contract's recorded balance for that caller strictly increases by exactly the sent amount; the mutant's swapped assert can cause deposit() to revert for some inputs (e.g., when addition overflow/ordering makes the assert fail) and thus violate this guarantee.

For any caller and any nonzero deposit amount that successfully sends Ether to deposit(), the reference contract always records the caller's balance increased by exactly the sent amount (so deposit returns/accepts and increases balances); the mutant's swapped assert can cause deposit() to revert for some inputs (some msg.value) and thus fail this universal property.

For any caller and any non-negative deposit value that is sent to deposit(), the reference contract always accepts the call and increases the caller's recorded balance by exactly the sent amount; the mutant's reordered assert can make deposit() revert for some msg.value, breaking this property.

For any caller and any uint256 deposit value, calling deposit() either (A) succeeds and increases the caller's recorded balance by exactly msg.value, or (B) reverts; the reference contract never reverts when sending a nonzero msg.value from an EOA and thus for any EOA and amount > 0 the call succeeds and balances[caller] increases by amount — the mutant can revert for some inputs causing this to fail.

For any caller address and any uint256 msgValue, if a caller (an EOA) sends msgValue > 0 to deposit(), the call always succeeds (does not revert) and afterwards address(c).balance increases by exactly msgValue; the mutant's reordered assert can make deposit() revert for some msgValue, violating this.
After depositing an amount, the caller's recorded balance (as inferred by a successful withdraw) is at least the sum of all their deposits made through deposit calls.
A deposit call should never revert (i.e., always succeed) for any nonzero msg.value sent to deposit.
If deposit is called with a positive ether value, the call must succeed (not revert).

Calling deposit with a positive value should not revert when the contract has enough balance to accept the msg.value (i.e., the caller's msg.value fits within uint256 addition without underflow in original but would cause negative update in mutant).
For any deposit amount > 0 the original contract never reverts the deposit call (reverted == false); the mutant can revert for some such inputs.

For any depositor and any positive msg.value, calling deposit() increases that depositor's balance in the contract (balance_after >= balance_before + msg.value); the mutant that subtracts msg.value can make the depositor's recorded balance decrease, violating this rule.

For any depositor and any nonzero deposit amount, after calling deposit() the recorded balance for that depositor increases by exactly the deposited amount (reference holds for all inputs; the mutant that subtracts msg.value can make the recorded balance decrease for some inputs).

For any depositor and any deposit value, invoking deposit() never decreases that depositor's recorded balance (balance_after >= balance_before); the mutant that subtracts msg.value can make the recorded balance decrease for some fuzzed amounts and actors.

For any depositor and any deposit amount, the contract's total ether balance (address(c).balance) always increases by exactly the sent msg.value when deposit() is invoked (the mutant that subtracts msg.value still receives the funds but corrupts the internal accounting, so address(c).balance change equals msg.value for both — instead we must observe a rule that the reference preserves: the sum of all stored balances equals address(c).balance; the mutant can break this by decreasing the stored per-user balance while the contract balance increases, so the invariant totalStoredBalances == address(c).balance holds for all inputs in the reference and is violated by the mutant),

For any depositor and any sequence where only deposit() is called, the contract's stored balance for that depositor never decreases (i.e., balances[depositor] after deposit >= balances[depositor] before); the mutant that subtracts msg.value can make the stored per-user balance decrease for some fuzzed depositor and amount.
After calling deposit with some nonzero value, the caller's balance in C increases by that value (i.e. address(c).balance and the recorded balance reflect the deposit).

Calling deposit with nonzero msg.value must not be a no-op: the call only succeeds (does not revert) when msg.value > 0 and the contract accepts the funds (i.e., deposit should not silently return without reverting when called with nonzero value).

For any nonzero ether amount sent to deposit, the original contract accepts the funds (call does not return immediately), so deposit reverts iff zero value is sent (i.e., deposit with value>0 does not revert).
If a caller sends >0 wei to deposit the call must not revert (i.e., deposit with a positive value always succeeds)
deposit with a positive attached value must not silently return: for any caller and any positive amount sent, the original contract's deposit call does not revert and therefore reverted == false.

For any caller and any positive deposit value, after calling deposit() the contract's recorded balance for that caller increases by exactly the sent amount (balances[msg.sender] == previous + value); the mutant returns early making deposit a no-op so this rule is violated for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero value sent, calling deposit() increases that caller's recorded balance by at least the sent amount (so balances[msg] after >= before + value); the mutant's early return makes deposit a no-op and thus violates this for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero ETH value, calling deposit() increases that caller's recorded balance by exactly the sent amount (balances[msg.sender] after == balances[msg.sender] before + value); the mutant's early return makes deposit a no-op so this equality can be violated for some fuzzed caller/amount.

For any caller and any positive ETH amount that the caller actually sends with deposit(), the contract's ether balance (address(c).balance) increases by exactly that amount; the mutant returns early so address(c).balance does not increase for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero ETH value they send, calling deposit() causes the contract's recorded per-caller balance (public getter balances) to increase strictly (i.e. balances[caller]_after > balances[caller]_before); the mutant's early return makes deposit a no-op so there exist inputs where this increase does not occur.
After depositing X and then calling withdraw(X), the caller's balance (address(this).balance) increases by X (i.e., full-balance withdrawals succeed).

property_summary: Withdrawing an amount equal to the caller's current balance must succeed (not revert).
If the caller attempts to withdraw an amount that is less than or equal to their current balance, the withdraw call does not revert.
If the caller tries to withdraw a non-zero amount and their balance is at least that amount, the call does not revert.
When amount > 0 and address(c).balance >= amount, withdraw must not revert.

For any depositor and deposit amount > 0, the reference contract allows a withdraw of exactly the depositor's full balance (i.e., withdrawing balance amount should succeed or be allowed), whereas the mutant that requires amount < balance disallows withdrawing the full balance for some inputs (when amount == balance).

For any depositor and any positive deposit value D, the reference contract allows a withdrawal of exactly D (withdrawing the full balance) whereas the mutant that uses require(amount < balance) forbids withdrawing the full balance when amount == balance.

For any depositor and any nonzero deposit amount, withdrawing exactly the depositor's entire balance is allowed by the reference C (withdraw(amount==balance) succeeds / does not revert) while the mutant that uses require(amount < balance) forbids withdrawing the full balance and thus will revert for some inputs where amount == balance.

For any depositor and any nonzero deposit D, attempting to withdraw exactly D (the depositor's full balance) either succeeds on the reference; the mutant that changes require(amount <= balances[msg.sender]) to require(amount < balances[msg.sender]) will revert when attempting to withdraw the full balance, so the rule is: withdrawing exactly your full balance should be allowed (i.e., not revert) — the mutant breaks this by rejecting amount == balance.

For any depositor and any deposit amount A > 0, attempting to withdraw an amount equal to the depositor's balance should succeed (not revert) on the reference contract; the mutant that requires amount < balance makes that call revert when amount == balance.

For any caller and any withdraw amount <= their balance, after a successful withdraw the contract's recorded balance for that caller equals the previous balance minus the withdrawn amount; the mutant subtracts an extra 1 wei and thus can make the post-withdraw recorded balance smaller by 1 for some inputs.

For any caller and any withdraw amount ≤ their recorded balance, the contract always sends exactly that amount out so that the contract's ether balance decreases by the withdrawn amount; the mutant sends one wei less than requested (creating a mismatch between recorded balance reduction and ether actually transferred) and thus can violate this invariant for some inputs.
